title: Members and encapsulation — one screen
rememberThis: A class variable holds a reference to a heap object — assignment copies the reference, not the object. A struct assignment copies the data.
Properties are the public API; keep fields private. C# 14 `field` keyword synthesizes the backing store inside an accessor.
Learn ordinary parameters first, then ref/in/out. Use `init` and `required` to pin construction. Finalizers are module 14. Extension members are module 10.
bullets: Default member accessibility is `private`; default type accessibility is `internal`. The `file` keyword limits a type to one source file.
Primary constructors (C# 12) capture parameters for the type body. `required` properties force object-initializer completeness at compile time.
`readonly struct` plus `in` parameters avoid defensive copies on hot paths (cache keys, coordinates).
`params` collections (C# 13) accept more than arrays. Operator overloading comes last; C# 14 adds user-defined compound assignment (`+=`).
